# Help improve the course materials

If a figure is difficult to read, an example produces an unexpected result, or
an explanation seems inconsistent, please raise it. A precise correction helps
the whole class and future readers of the course.

The instructor maintains this repository to distribute reviewed course PDFs.
Students and independent readers can help by identifying errors, unclear
passages, broken links, or differences between a class's slides and notes.

## Where to send a correction

Enrolled students can use the course Microsoft Teams space for questions or
corrections that can be discussed with the class. Keep unreleased assessment
solutions and individual circumstances out of that channel.

Email Prof. Gabriel Spadon at [spadon@dal.ca](mailto:spadon@dal.ca) for a private
question or a correction that would reveal your assessed work. Enrolled students
should use their Dalhousie email. Independent readers are welcome to email
corrections through the same address.

If you find personal information or an accidentally published private file,
follow the [confidential reporting guidance](SECURITY.md).

## Make the issue easy to locate

A useful report includes the details needed to check it.

1. Name the teaching week, Class A or B, and the document title. Include the
   PDF link and page or slide number.
2. Identify the passage, equation, figure, table, or example in question. If you
   downloaded a copy, note that so it can be compared with the current release.
3. Explain what seems wrong or unclear and what you expected instead. Include a
   supporting source or a small calculation when it helps.
4. For a code example, state whether you used R or Python, the relevant input,
   and the observed output or error. Include software versions if they appear
   relevant. Keep any reproduction free of personal data and assessment answers.
5. If the slides and notes disagree, point to both locations. A correction may
   need to be reflected in the explanation, diagram, and worked example together.

You do not need to supply a replacement document or know the answer before
asking. Explaining where you became uncertain is useful feedback too.

## How corrections fit the course

The instructor checks reported issues against the source material and syllabus
before revising the released documents. Suggestions about wording or examples
do not change assessment weights, deadlines, or requirements. Follow the
[syllabus](../assets/planning/syllabus.pdf) and announcements for your offering.

Assessed work belongs in your own private repository and the announced
submission channel. Do not submit labs or assignments through issues or pull
requests in this teaching-materials repository. Use the
[portfolio workflow](../README.md#your-data-science-portfolio) for submitting a
fixed version and sharing it after release.
